source.scope_guardrail: Only the supplied Discord corpus was used. No web, chart, market, or outside instructional knowledge was used to fill missing mechanics.
source.dedupe_policy: Count by Discord message_id. When the same message_id appeared in more than one source array, contextual_qa_messages was preferred for reply/answer text because it is the later reply-linked capture.

interpretation_rules.documented_recurring: The corpus explicitly names the model or supplies an operational checklist, and the workflow appears in more than one message or journal instance.
interpretation_rules.provisional_derived: The workflow recurs, but the model name or full sequence is assembled from multiple Discord messages rather than stated as one canonical checklist.
interpretation_rules.exact_excerpt: A verbatim substring of content_text from the specified message. Typos and capitalization are intentionally preserved.
evidence_strength_order: reply-linked answer from a named mentor/moderator
same-author detailed journal with stated outcome
interpretation_rules.outcome_warning: Journal labels are self-reported and screenshots were not independently reconstructed. Keyword counts are not setup counts, trade counts, or win-rate statistics.

models.name: 10AM key-open rejection model
models.why_materially_distinct: The corpus repeatedly calls this a separate 10AM model, requires interaction with the 10AM key open, and distinguishes later generic RB trades from the time-boxed key-open setup.

eligibility_context.rule: A directional bias or draw should already exist; the 10AM line by itself is not enough.
Prefer the key open to overlap at least one meaningful PDA or range feature; one explicit checklist asks for two or more among FVG, OB, RB, and OTE.
Under Domme's answer, wait for a full tap of 10AM and stop considering new 10AM entries at 11AM.

identification.instruction: Mark the 10AM key open and establish whether the setup is a long-from-discount or short-from-premium idea using the existing bias/draw.
Look for a manipulation/sweep around 10AM into a PDA such as a 5m or 15m FVG/RB/OB or OTE.
Require price to fully tap the 10AM level for the strict variant; a nearby RB that does not tap the line is treated as a different or failed eligibility case in the cited journal.
Use either a direct key-open limit variant or a closed trigger variant. The closed trigger is commonly a 5m RB/CISD; a 1m RB/CISD is used for tighter risk only when structure is clean.

trigger.primary_documented: Closed 5m RB or CISD after the 10AM/PDA reaction; the trigger must be closed, not still forming.
trigger.alternate_documented: Limit at the 10AM key open after the setup has the required context; several journals then monitor a 1m RB or use a 1m trigger for risk refinement.
trigger.lower_timeframe_caveat: The corpus repeatedly describes 1m entries as tighter but easier to edge or stop; Domme rejected one poor-looking 1m RB and preferred a higher-timeframe formation in that instance.

required_or_near_required_in_documented_: full interaction with the 10AM key open for the strict variant
a closed reversal trigger when not using the direct-limit variant
high_value: FVG, OB, RB, or OTE overlapping 10AM
not_sufficient_by_itself: the 10AM line without HTF bias/PDA context
an RB near but not actually tapping 10AM in the strict variant

invalidation.condition: No full 10AM tap under the strict Domme/Liam variant.
After 11AM, Domme stops looking for the 10AM setup.
Stop beyond the structure that makes the reversal wrong; no single universal number is stated.
No HTF bias/PDA, entry inside chop, or the intended draw already delivered.

entry: Direct limit at the fully tapped 10AM key open is documented in Liam's journal.
Closed 5m RB/CISD is the default trigger in Anton's checklist.
A 1m RB/CISD or 1m FVG inside a larger wick is a risk-refinement variant, not a universal requirement.
stop: Above/below the structure where the idea is wrong.
A lower-timeframe trigger may tighten the stop, but the corpus reports frequent edging and premature stop-outs.
target: Nearest meaningful swing or opposing liquidity is documented more consistently than a fixed multiple.
One journal states the first swing high was 110 points and 1:5R and was sufficient; holding for all engineered liquidity converted the trade to breakeven.
management: Trailing below/above the 1m RB is used by some journals but caused a stopped trade in one otherwise accepted setup.
No corpus-wide scaling rule was established.
missing_or_not_universal: whether every setup should use a limit or an entry trigger

time_scope.timezone_caveat: Messages use 10AM/10:00 and U.S. index-session language, but the extracted text does not consistently declare a timezone. The value is stored exactly as the Discord authors stated it.

instrument_scope.usage: NQ/MNQ is often the traded chart and ES is frequently used for SMT/reference; some authors also execute on ES.
instrument_scope.comparative_claim: No controlled NQ-versus-ES win-rate comparison exists in the corpus.

failed_or_contradictory_evidence.finding: A 10AM-aligned 5m bearish FVG plus 1m CISD failed immediately when the trader lacked HTF bias/PDA and entered chop.
A setup with CPI/data-low sweep, SMT, 0.5, 15m gap fill, and 5m bearish closures still produced a small loss after the stop was trailed behind a 1m RB.
A 5m FVG/RB entry that did not tap 10AM stopped; re-entry at 10AM worked, but over-ambitious targeting turned it into breakeven.
Domme answered 'No' when asked whether he would use a 10m-chart RB for the 10AM 4hr-expansion example.

models.name: HTF PDA rejection into lower-timeframe RB entry
models.why_materially_distinct: This is the recurring non-10AM RB workflow. It starts from any meaningful HTF PDA/liquidity event and uses a lower-timeframe RB or related entry trigger; it is not tied to one key-open clock.

eligibility_context.rule: The candidate RB must reject something meaningful—commonly an FVG, OB, liquidity pool, or another HTF PDA—not merely be a visually convenient wick.
The directional bias and target must remain active; a technically valid RB after the daily draw has already delivered is not a fresh trade thesis.
Prefer correct premium/discount and an unmitigated level; avoid a long RB already in premium or an RB that has already been mitigated.

identification.instruction: Locate the HTF PDA or liquidity event that the rejection is reacting from.

Identify the candle/wick that starts the rejection. One detailed 4h example was a swing low with a wick whose prior candle had a higher low; Domme also confirmed a construction caused by a volume imbalance.
Wait for the RB to close before treating it as an entry trigger.
If the parent RB is too large, refine inside it with a 1m/3m RB, CISD, FVG, or breaker; do not invent a stop in the middle of the wick merely to fit risk.

trigger.primary_documented: Closed RB at the selected timeframe after the PDA/liquidity reaction.
refinement_variants: CE or OTE retracement of the RB
1m or 3m RB inside a larger 5m/15m wick
trigger.timeframe_note: The corpus repeatedly uses 1m, 3m, 5m, and 15m RBs. Domme explicitly answered 'No' to using a 10m RB in the cited 10AM example; no universal ban outside that example was established.

conditional_or_optional: A one- or two-tick sweep can still qualify; Domme and boy both answered that a sweep is a sweep.
The prior candle color is not consistently treated as mandatory; Haks calls it a preference, while Domme confirms examples by close and volume imbalance.
low_probability_signals: random wick with no rejected level
RB at the beginning of an unfilled imbalance
entry after the target/daily draw has already delivered

invalidation.condition: The RB is already mitigated before the proposed entry.
The RB is merely a random wick, rejects no meaningful level, or begins an unfilled imbalance.
The intended draw has already delivered or the trade would enter on the wrong premium/discount side.
The structural extreme/wick that defines the RB fails. The corpus supports placing the stop beyond the full structure, but does not supply one universal close-versus-wick invalidation rule.

entry: CE/start/OTE of the parent RB is used by several journals.
A closed 1m/3m RB, CISD, FVG, or breaker inside a larger 5m/15m RB is used for tighter risk.
stop: Do not place a meaningless stop in the middle of a large wick solely to force the desired size.
target: Remaining draw, opposing liquidity, a key open, or the next swing/PDA.
No single fixed target rule is shared by all authors.
management: Lower-timeframe refinement can improve nominal R but increases edge-out risk.
The corpus contains valid-looking RBs that still stopped before a later RB delivered; re-entry is author-specific and not standardized.

time_scope.documented: No single fixed time defines the generic RB model. Examples occur at market open, after 10AM, and in London-session discussion.
time_scope.separation_from_M1: If the trade depends on a full 10AM key-open tap and occurs before the 11AM cutoff, classify it as M1; otherwise retain it here as generic RB.
time_scope.timezone_caveat: Session labels are kept as written because the extracted messages do not consistently declare timezone.

instrument_scope.cross_market_use: NQ and ES are often read together for SMT; either can host the PDA/RB and either can be the execution instrument in member journals.
instrument_scope.comparative_claim: The corpus does not establish that RBs work better on NQ than ES or provide denominator-based results by instrument.

failed_or_contradictory_evidence.finding: A 3m RB that hit a 15m FVG and 5m OTE was called valid but still wicked through before a later 1m RB moved higher.
Two bullish 5m RB entries after a sweep/0.705 both stopped because the wick was too large and the stops were placed meaninglessly inside it; the trader later judged the HTF narrative ambiguous.
A technically identifiable RB was dismissed as a new trade because price had already delivered to the daily low.
Candle-color geometry is not perfectly consistent across the corpus; one author prefers a prior sell candle for bullish RBs but still considers a same-color example valid.

models.name: MMXM/LABS with STDV reversal zone and breaker entry
models.why_materially_distinct: Two explicit strategy posts name MMXM/LABS and define an AMD/PO3, STDV, TFA, HTF-PDA, and breaker workflow. It is a staged market-model and deviation framework rather than an RB-only setup.

eligibility_context.rule: Align HTF and LTF bias and use AMD/PO3 or MMXM as the narrative framework.
Use D/4H HRL and HTF PD arrays for direction/reversal, 15m FVG as a common rejection area, premium/discount for POI selection, and STDV for reversal/target zones.
SMT is a bonus in one explicit strategy, but confirmation and a liquidity sweep become important when NQ/ES are decorrelated or price is consolidating.

identification.instruction: Map the higher-timeframe direction and PDA, then label the current AMD/PO3 or MMXM stage.
Use TFA such as 4H/15M/1M or 1D/1H/5M and locate the 15m FVG or other HTF rejection zone in correct premium/discount.
Use STDV to identify the anticipated reversal zone and projected objectives.
Wait for the appropriate MMXM/PO3 low-risk stage or a confirmed breaker and retest.

trigger.primary_documented: Breaker entry after the model and reversal zone are established.
trigger.named_answer: boy answered that the entry trigger is a 'Low risk buy off a mmxm or any stage po3'.
trigger.alternate_documented: If the same TFA permits acceptable risk, use an OTE retracement and PDA; one journal missed the breaker and entered the range retest.

low_probability_conditions: missing the traded instrument's own STDV

invalidation.condition: HTF direction contradicts the proposed bias or price action reclassifies into the opposite MMXM direction.
Breaker is front-run or no confirmed breakout/retest occurs in consolidation.
NQ and ES are decorrelated and the selected instrument has not reached its own STDV/liquidity condition.
Stop beyond the breaker structure/ranges; exact placement varies by journal.

entry: OTE plus PDA when the TFA supplies acceptable risk
stop: One detailed winning example covered both breaker ranges.
No universal point/tick stop exists in the corpus.
target: One explicit strategy uses -2 or -2.5 STDV as main breaker targets and -4 for a runner.
Another explicit plan requires at least 3R; an earlier plan states desired R:R of 2+.
management: One strategy trails to breakeven only after the breaker is mitigated and after its stated initial target.
One-win/one-loss lockout rules are trader-specific, not model mechanics.
missing_or_not_universal: directional sign convention for STDV across long and short examples

documented: Asia/London can form the accumulation/manipulation context.
Market open and 10AM PO3 appear in execution examples.
One personal plan says '8:30/9 FINISHED'; the timezone is not stated.
One trader reports poor results around '7:30', but that is anecdotal and not a server-wide rule.
time_scope.timezone_caveat: Clock labels are stored as written and are not normalized.

instrument_scope.usage: NQ and ES are jointly evaluated for SMT, STDV, and decorrelation. An MNQ NY-AM win is also recorded.
instrument_scope.comparative_claim: No instrument-specific expectancy can be calculated from the available self-reported examples.

failed_or_contradictory_evidence.finding: One trader explicitly says LABS has lower probability in consolidation and logged 2 BE plus 2 losses, even though breakers/FVG alignment and SMT were present.
A first trade lost because NQ had not reached its own STDV and had no liquidity sweep; a confirmed breaker retest in the same journal was the winning trade.
Three of four trades lost in another journal day; one conflicted with HTF direction and two front-ran the breaker, while the 15m RB plus 1m breaker near STDV 4 was the win.
SMT is explicitly optional in one strategy but treated as important confirmation in decorrelated conditions elsewhere; it is therefore a context-dependent filter, not a universal requirement.

models.name: NY-open/macro sweep, displacement, and FVG retest
models.why_materially_distinct: This recurring journal workflow waits for the NY open or named macro, uses a Judas/liquidity sweep and structure displacement, then enters a retracement into a newly created FVG/iFVG. RBs can support the POI, but the mandatory confirmation is displacement/structure rather than an RB alone.

eligibility_context.rule: Start with HTF direction, an unresolved liquidity target, and a specific manipulation zone such as a 15m/1h FVG, OTE, session high/low, or HTF liquidity.
Wait for the open/macro sweep or Judas move; do not chase an already extended move without a fresh reversal structure.
Require clean confirmation when SMT is conflicted, the market is choppy, or news is active.

identification.instruction: At NY open or the named macro, identify a liquidity sweep/Judas move into the preselected HTF or 15m PDA.
Wait for CISD/BOS plus displacement away from the sweep; a weak or unclosed lower-timeframe signal is not enough.
Mark the new 1m FVG/iFVG, breaker, or overlapping 5m RB/1m OB created by the displacement.
Enter on the retrace/retest only after the structure has actually flipped or confirmed continuation.

trigger.primary_documented: Retest of a 1m FVG/iFVG after BOS/CISD and displacement.
trigger.alternate_documented: A confirmed breaker retest or 30s iFVG after an external HTF liquidity sweep and SMT.
trigger.lower_timeframe_caveat: A 30s inverse taken before the candle closed and without strong displacement lost; 30s is therefore evidence-supported only as a refined, confirmed trigger, not a standalone early signal.

required_in_observed_sequence: retrace into the created entry array

invalidation.condition: The trigger candle does not close with strong displacement or no BOS/CISD occurs.
Stop beyond the swept low/high or structure used for the entry; examples use stops at the lows for longs.
The expected sweep never occurs, both sides print conflicting SMT, or the opposite structure becomes more compelling after the initial trade fails.
News or chop prevents clean delivery; the corpus contains stops and breakevens despite otherwise coherent structure.

entry: 30s iFVG only after external sweep/SMT and confirmed close
stop: At the swept low/high or beyond the entry structure in the cited examples.
target: fixed R targets used in examples include 1:3, 2.08R, 2.78R, and 5R; these are outcomes/examples, not one canonical target rule.
management: Another accepted breakeven after being up 60 points in a choppy second macro.
No shared trailing rule is established.

time_scope.documented_window_label: NY open and the author's named macro/second macro
time_scope.timezone_caveat: The detailed posts do not define the macro's exact clock boundaries, so this artifact does not import an outside definition.

instrument_scope.usage: NQ is frequently the execution or liquidity-sweep chart and ES supplies SMT confirmation; at least one detailed fractal example chose ES for execution while referencing NQ.
instrument_scope.comparative_claim: No controlled performance comparison supports preferring NQ over ES.

failed_or_contradictory_evidence.finding: A 30s inverse before the candle closed lost; the later move needed a lower sweep followed by BOS and displacement.
A .705 OTE plus data lows, 15m FVG, and bullish SMT still stopped because the trader entered without waiting for 1m BOS/displacement confirmation.
A second-macro reversal reached +60 points and then stopped at breakeven in chop.

A separate fractal example's first 1m FVG/breaker trade stopped because the swing was weak, a 15m OB was ignored, index confirmation was weak, and the candle was effectively a doji; the later 15m-CISD then 1m-CISD setup won.

highest_probability_profile_from_corpus: Bias/draw is explicit and not already delivered.
The setup reacts from a meaningful HTF PDA or liquidity event.
The entry is on the correct premium/discount side.
Liquidity is swept before the reversal/continuation trigger.
NQ/ES SMT supports rather than conflicts with the trade.
The RB/CISD/breaker closes and shows real displacement.
The level is fresh/unmitigated and is not the beginning of an unfilled imbalance.
The stop covers the structure instead of being forced inside a large wick.
The target remains open and is close enough to justify the trade.
lowest_probability_profile_from_corpus: Random or isolated 1m RB with no rejected level.
No HTF bias/PDA or entry inside chop.
Wrong premium/discount side or target already delivered.
Already-mitigated RB or RB at the beginning of an unfilled imbalance.
NQ/ES decorrelation that is not resolved by the setup.
Stop placed inside a large wick solely to force risk.
Entry before a required 10AM tap or after the 11AM cutoff for the strict 10AM model.
Trading through unstable news/chop without fresh confirmation.

nq_vs_es.supported: The corpus repeatedly uses NQ/MNQ and ES together. SMT and relative strength are core filters, and some authors execute on NQ/MNQ while using ES as confirmation; others select ES when it is moving faster.
nq_vs_es.not_supported: There is no denominator-based instrument sample, controlled backtest, or consistent trade ledger proving that rejection blocks work better on NQ than ES.
nq_vs_es.operational_database_answer: Treat both as supported examples and store execution_instrument separately from reference_instrument; instrument superiority is unknown from this corpus.

time_findings.strongest_recurring_clock: 10AM key open, with a named cutoff at 11AM in Domme's answer.
other_recurring_contexts: 3-5AM if trading London in one Domme reply
time_findings.caveat: Only 10AM has enough repeated, operational detail to stand alone as a time-based model. Exact timezone normalization was not inferred.

not_promoted_to_standalone_models.reason: Only one fully detailed paired loss/win post explicitly names the fractal model. Its mechanics are preserved as a confirmation variant inside M4 rather than overstated as a fifth independent recurring model.
SMT recurs as a confluence and relative-market filter, but the corpus does not support SMT alone as a complete entry/stop/target model.
The term appears in one detailed loss/BE journal and lacks enough independent operational examples in this 14-day corpus.
The phrase appears, but the captured messages do not provide a complete, consistent rule set separate from M1 and M2.

limitations: The broad server-wide RB shorthand search was partial after 325 captured results, so server-wide frequency is a lower-bound/biased sample.
Search results over-sample messages containing RB/rejection terminology and under-sample relevant messages that use only images or different shorthand.
Many trade posts depend on screenshots; this analysis does not infer unseen price geometry from attachment filenames.
Self-reported wins, losses, R multiples, and retrospective labels were not independently verified against market data.
Some reply-linked messages have blank captured authors; named-answer claims are used only where the contextual record includes the author.
The corpus covers 14 observed calendar days, not 30 days.
The database deliberately leaves unresolved mechanics as unknown rather than importing outside ICT definitions.
This is a research extraction, not a claim of profitability or financial advice.
